originalTitle: Lindsay Clancy had ‘thoughts of harming the children’, her mother testifies at trial
summary: Paula Musgrove stated her daughter had said medications were ‘destroying’ her mind and she was becoming ‘paranoid’
content: The defense in the Lindsay Clancy filicide case called the defendant’s mother as one of its first witnesses Monday, after three weeks of prosecution evidence laid out, in often harrowing detail, events surrounding Clancy’s killing of her three children. Under questioning from defense attorney David Reddington, Clancy’s mother, Paula Musgrove, testified that her daughter’s statements and actions had unsettled her in the months leading up to 24 January 2023. Clancy, Musgrove testified to the court in Plymouth, Massachusetts, had asked if she could sleep in her mother’s bed and told her she felt the medication she had been prescribed for postpartum depression were “destroying” her mind. Musgrove also disclosed that on one occasion her daughter had approached her and Lindsay’s former husband, Patrick Clancy, and said: “I want to tell you guys something”. “She said she had thoughts of harming the children,” Musgrove testified. Patrick has previously told the court of his former wife’s statement and said she told him she had no plans to hurt the kids. Jurors have heard testimony from Patrick that his wife told him after the killings, while in hospital, that she’d “heard a man’s voice telling her that if she didn’t do it now, she would lose her chance, or something like that”. Lindsay’s mother also said she received a text from her daughter on 20 October, three months before the killings. “I’m really sick. Something is wrong,” Lindsay wrote, saying she didn’t know how she would get through each day, and that medicine had not helped. “I don’t want to be alone,” Lindsay added in the text. Musgrove went to her daughter’s home in Duxbury, Massachusetts, and stayed for a week. In the following months, Musgrove and her husband made repeated trips from their home in Connecticut. “In November and December, it was not getting better,” Musgrove testified, adding that Lindsay was losing weight and becoming “paranoid”. Musgrove said her daughter had said “this wasn’t her mind” and said “this isn’t me. I just want to feel better and enjoy my kids again.” Lindsay’s defense is seeking to show she was suffering from a broad array of depressive symptoms, for which she had sought psychiatric help in the months leading up to the killing. Reddington argues the killings were driven by postpartum mental illness and not an intentional act, as prosecutors contend, followed by an insincere suicide attempt. Lindsay, 36, is charged with the murders of her children, Cora, five, Dawson, three and eight-month-old Callan. Lindsay does not deny she fatally strangled her children – but has pleaded not guilty to murder, by reason of insanity or, under Massachusetts statutes, a lack of criminal responsibility. If convicted of first-degree murder Lindsay faces life in prison without parole. If jurors find her not guilty, due to lack of criminal responsibility or by reason of insanity, she would be committed to a state psychiatric hospital. Allison Ozga, Lindsay’s sister, testified that in the months leading up to the killings she had learned that her sister was having suicidal thoughts. “She’s feeling numb, she’s feeling hopeless,” Ozga said. Earlier on Monday, the prosecution rested after calling Ian Whiffin, ‌a digital forensic expert tasked with examining Lindsay’s cellphone to look at her search history, ‌calls, text messages and health data. Whiffin said that at 5pm on the night of the killings, Lindsay had climbed two flights of stairs and spoken by phone with her husband, who was then at a pharmacy collecting constipation medication and going to pick up a takeout. In the days prior, Whiffin testified, Lindsay searched online for “how quickly does Wellbutrin work for depression”, giving a brand name for a medication used to treat major depression, and “ketamine for suicidal ideation”. Five days before killing the children, on 19 January, she searched “symptoms of postpartum psychosis” and “psychosis symptoms”.
chineseTitle: 林赛·克兰西的母亲在审判中作证说，她有“伤害孩子的想法”
chineseSummary: 宝拉·穆斯格罗夫 (Paula Musgrove) 表示，她的女儿曾表示药物正在“摧毁”她的思想，她变得“偏执”
chineseContent: 林赛·克兰西杀妻案的辩方周一称被告的母亲为首批证人之一，此前三周的检方证据经常以令人痛心的细节列出了围绕克兰西杀害三个孩子的事件。在辩护律师大卫·雷丁顿 (David Reddington) 的询问下，克兰西的母亲保拉·穆斯格罗夫 (Paula Musgrove) 作证说，在 2023 年 1 月 24 日之前的几个月里，女儿的言论和行为让她感到不安。克兰西·穆斯格罗夫在马萨诸塞州普利茅斯的法庭作证时，曾问她是否可以睡在母亲的床上，并告诉她，她觉得为她开的治疗产后抑郁症的药物正在“摧毁”她的思想。穆斯格罗夫还透露，有一次她的女儿曾接近她和林赛的前夫帕特里克·克兰西，并说：“我想告诉你们一件事”。 “她说她有伤害孩子们的想法，”穆斯格罗夫作证说。帕特里克此前曾向法庭讲述了他前妻的声明，并表示她告诉他她没有计划伤害孩子们。陪审员们听取了帕特里克的证词，他的妻子在杀人事件发生后在医院告诉他，她“听到一个男人的声音告诉她，如果她现在不这样做，她就会失去机会，或者类似的事情”。林赛的母亲还表示，她于 10 月 20 日收到女儿发来的短信，即案发前三个月。 “我真的病了。出了什么问题，”林赛写道，她不知道自己该如何度过每一天，而且药物也没有帮助。 “我不想孤单，”林赛在短信中补充道。穆斯格罗夫前往她女儿位于马萨诸塞州达克斯伯里的家，并在那里呆了一个星期。在接下来的几个月里，穆斯格罗夫和她的丈夫多次从康涅狄格州的家出发。 “在
